title: Sqrt(x)
prompt: Given a non-negative integer `x`, return the square root of `x` rounded down to the nearest integer. You may not use any built-in exponent or square root function; compute it yourself.

examples.explanation: sqrt(8) is approximately 2.828, which truncates down to 2.

hints: Testing every integer from 0 upward until its square exceeds x works but is O(sqrt(x)) time.
The function f(k) = k*k is monotonically increasing for k >= 0, so you can binary search on the answer itself instead of scanning.
Search for the largest integer k such that k*k <= x; keep narrowing low/high and remember the best k found so far, since exact equality may never occur.

solution.approach: Binary search over the candidate answer space [0, x]. For a candidate mid, if mid*mid <= x it's a valid (possibly not tight) answer, so record it and try a larger mid by moving low up; otherwise mid is too big and high moves down. This works because k*k is monotonic in k, so the set of valid k forms a contiguous prefix of the search space, letting binary search find its boundary in O(log x) time.
